title: a variable named _copy was a plain assignment, so freeing it destroyed the original
object: the profile directory path string from get_persconffile_dir, a g_strdup
lifetime_ender: g_free(pf_dir_path_copy), where pf_dir_path_copy is an ALIAS of pf_dir_path, not a copy
shape: an alias whose name says copy, so freeing it destroys the original
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `ws_mkdir(pf_dir_path, 0755)` on the very next statement.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8:wsutil/filesystem.c carries `pf_dir_path_copy = g_strdup(pf_dir_path);` (`grep -c` = 1). The plain-assignment form is at 012a179785ab^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.
nested_why: the object came straight from g_malloc / g_new / g_new0 / g_strdup / getline -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no wmem allocator between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../wmem-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the defect is in the NAME: `pf_dir_path_copy = pf_dir_path` makes the two variables one allocation, so a reader checking that the copy is freed sees correct-looking code. The fix is to make the copy real, `g_strdup(pf_dir_path)` -- not to move or remove a free -- and the freed pointer is then also RETURNED to the caller, which frees it again.
